notes:
Three licensing defects, and the one that mattered most was a question that cost money.

**Asking whether you were activated used to spend an activation.** The status
form of `docket licence` — no key typed, just the question — ran the full
activation path, and where this Mac held no seat it could prove, it took one to
answer. A licence covers three Macs. Anything that marked the cached result
invalid, then you checking your own status, spent one. Three checks and the
licence was exhausted on a machine you never left. Status is now a read: it
confirms a seat you already hold and otherwise tells you to activate.

**A build could trust a licence check another build had earned.** The cached
validation in `~/.docket` was keyed on the licence key alone, so one successful
check bought twenty-four hours of "Licensed" for whatever asked next with the
same key, and up to fourteen days of offline grace on top. It is now keyed on
the build that earned it as well.

**And the test suite could quietly talk to a payment provider.** Its own first
line promised every input was built in memory; nothing enforced it. Network
access now raises in tests unless a test declares that it means it, so the set
of tests that contact a vendor is written down instead of assumed.

Nothing in your audits changes in this release.
